dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 王明，你的房间在哪儿？
dialogue.pinyin: Wáng Míng, nǐ de fángjiān zài nǎr?
dialogue.english: Wang Ming, where's your room?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 在左边。小美的房间在我的房间旁边。
dialogue.pinyin: Zài zuǒbian. Xiǎoměi de fángjiān zài wǒ de fángjiān pángbiān.
dialogue.english: On the left. Xiaomei's room is next to mine.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 你的房间真大！桌子上的书都是你的吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ de fángjiān zhēn dà! Zhuōzi shang de shū dōu shì nǐ de ma?
dialogue.english: Your room is really big! Are all the books on the desk yours?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不都是。这些是我的，那些是我爸爸的。
dialogue.pinyin: Bù dōu shì. Zhèxiē shì wǒ de, nàxiē shì wǒ bàba de.
dialogue.english: Not all of them. These are mine, and those are my dad's.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 小美在她的房间吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Xiǎoměi zài tā de fángjiān ma?
dialogue.english: Is Xiaomei in her room?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不在，她和我妈妈去商店了。
dialogue.pinyin: Bú zài, tā hé wǒ māma qù shāngdiàn le.
dialogue.english: No, she went to the shops with my mom.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 安娜，这些衣服真漂亮！是你的吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Ānnà, zhèxiē yīfu zhēn piàoliang! Shì nǐ de ma?
dialogue.english: Anna, these clothes are really pretty! Are they yours?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不是我的，是小美的。我想送她。
dialogue.pinyin: Bú shì wǒ de, shì Xiǎoměi de. Wǒ xiǎng sòng tā.
dialogue.english: They're not mine, they're for Xiaomei. I want to give them to her.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 都是粉色的！
dialogue.pinyin: Dōu shì fěnsè de!
dialogue.english: They're all pink!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是啊，小美最喜欢粉色。她的杯子也是粉的。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, Xiǎoměi zuì xǐhuan fěnsè. Tā de bēizi yě shì fěn de.
dialogue.english: Yes, pink is Xiaomei's favorite color. Even her cup is pink.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 那这个红的呢？
dialogue.pinyin: Nà zhège hóng de ne?
dialogue.english: And what about this red one?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 红的是我的！
dialogue.pinyin: Hóng de shì wǒ de!
dialogue.english: The red one is mine!

newWords.english: (after a verb) a little, briefly; softens a request

title.english: The "的" Phrase Standing for a Noun

explanation.hanzi: 名词、代词、形容词或者动词短语后面加"的"，可以代替前面说过的或者大家都知道的名词。比如"红色的"就是"红色的手表"，"我的"就是"我的书"。
explanation.english: When everyone already knows what thing you mean, you can drop the noun and keep only the description + 的. 红色的 = "the red one", 我的 = "mine", 昨天买的 = "the one (I) bought yesterday". The description can be a color, a pronoun, a noun or a whole verb phrase. The 的 phrase works like a noun: it can be a subject (红的是我的) or come after 是 (这块手表是新的).

examples.hanzi: 红的是我的，粉的是小美的。
examples.pinyin: Hóng de shì wǒ de, fěn de shì Xiǎoměi de.
examples.english: The red one is mine, and the pink one is Xiaomei's.

examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài shǒubiǎo shì xīn de.
examples.english: This watch is a new one.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū shì wǒ zuótiān mǎi de.
examples.english: This book is the one I bought yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 你的杯子在桌子上，我的呢？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de bēizi zài zhuōzi shang, wǒ de ne?
examples.english: Your cup is on the table. Where's mine?

explanation.hanzi: "一下"放在动词后面，表示动作时间短，或者只是试一试。用在请求里，语气更客气、更轻松。
explanation.english: 一下 (yíxià) after a verb makes the action short and casual: 看一下 "take a quick look", 休息一下 "rest for a bit". In requests it softens the tone, so 你看一下 sounds friendlier than a bare 你看. An object comes after 一下: 看一下报纸.

examples.pinyin: Nín kàn yíxià zhè kuài shǒubiǎo.
examples.english: Have a look at this watch.
I'd like to rest for a bit.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ shuō yíxià nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Could you please tell us your name?

explanation.hanzi: "真＋形容词"表示感叹，说话人觉得程度很高，常常用在感叹句里。"真＋形容词"一般不放在名词前面做定语，这时要用"很"。
explanation.english: 真 (zhēn) + adjective is an exclamation: "How...!", "really...!". It shows the speaker's own surprise or feeling, so it is common in sentences ending with "!". Use it as the predicate only: 这件衣服真漂亮！ To describe a noun directly, use 很 instead: 很漂亮的衣服, not 真漂亮的衣服.

singleComponentChars.etymology: An open hand: the curved stroke is the arm and wrist, and the strokes crossing it are the spread fingers.

singleComponentChars.meaning: a unit of length (about 3.3 m); a respectful word for a grown man
singleComponentChars.etymology: A hand holding a measuring stick: it first meant a measure of length. Because a grown man was thought of as about one 丈 tall, it also came to refer to adult men, as in 丈夫.
A standing person (大) with an extra line across the head: the hairpin a young man wore once he came of age. So 夫 is a grown man, and later a husband.

radicals.english: tree, wood (related to trees and things made of wood)
standing knife (related to cutting and dividing)

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组，说说你的东西和颜色。
prompt.english: In pairs, talk about your things and their colors.

activities: Whose is it? Put a few classmates' things on a desk. Point and ask 这个是谁的？ and answer with a 的 phrase: 红色的是安娜的，粉的是……的.
Gift shopping: one partner is a shop assistant, the other wants to buy a present (送妈妈 / 送丈夫 / 送朋友). Use 看一下, 什么颜色, and prices with 千.
Draw your room: describe it to your partner with 左边、旁边 and 房间 while they draw it, then react with 真……！
Morning routine: tell your partner what a family member does every morning (起床, 喝牛奶, 看一下报纸).
